title: The Morning Brief: 49ers and Rays open the postseason calendar; criminal probes and contract talks shape the weekend
dek: The 49ers won the first NFL regular season game ever played in Australia, drawing 100,021 fans in Melbourne. The Rays clinched the first playoff berth of 2026 on Saturday. Off the field, federal prosecutors opened a criminal investigation into the Clippers' salary-cap practices, and LSU averted SEC expulsion by removing two former NFL players from its roster.
author: GoCheckMySports
key_fact: Saturday brought the collision of four distinct stories: the NFL's successful expansion into Australia, the Rays' clinching in a tight AL East race, federal criminal scrutiny of an NBA franchise, and a college football crisis paused but unresolved. The common thread is that September 11-12 settled some questions definitively while leaving others in suspension, the 49ers won their international game, the Rays reached October, the Clippers face indictment, and LSU remains in legal limbo.
bottom_line: Saturday opened three separate legal proceedings: the federal criminal investigation into the Clippers, the paused but unresolved SEC-LSU standoff, and LeShon Johnson's entry into federal custody. The Rays clinched a playoff berth and the 49ers won in Australia, two settled facts that frame a postseason calendar now in motion. The Clippers' prosecution timeline, the SEC's next move against LSU, and the outcome of the October playoff races will determine whether the coming weeks settle the remaining questions or defer them further.
body: The NFL played its first regular season game on Australian soil on Friday, as the San Francisco 49ers defeated the Los Angeles Rams at the Melbourne Cricket Ground before a sell-out crowd of 100,021 fans drawn from more than 30 countries. The event marks the start of a four-year agreement between the NFL and Melbourne, though the league has not committed to an annual game and the attendance and global reach suggest the arrangement will be tested by the AFL finals calendar and the league's competing scheduling demands in years to come. On the same evening, Kyle Shanahan's 49ers extended the head coach with a multiyear contract after his recovery from a July car crash, signaling continuity after two Super Bowl berths in his tenure.

The postseason arrived early for one AL team on Saturday. The Tampa Bay Rays defeated the Houston Astros 3-1, with Junior Caminero hitting a walk-off home run to clinch a playoff berth and end a three-year postseason drought. The Rays became the first team in 2026 to secure October play. The club's clinching comes despite middle-of-the-pack offensive production; the pitching staff, anchored by ace Drew Rasmussen and built for excellence in short bursts, is the structural foundation of a team that will play at least 16 more regular-season games before the postseason bracket begins in late September.

Off the field, two investigations moved forward in parallel. Federal prosecutors in Brooklyn opened a criminal probe into the Los Angeles Clippers, owner Steve Ballmer, and Kawhi Leonard for alleged salary-cap circumvention through third-party endorsement deals, escalating what was already the NBA's harshest enforcement action from league penalties into potential federal criminal territory. The investigation follows an NBA inquiry by the law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz that found the Clippers violated salary-cap rules by initiating off-court income opportunities for Leonard. In college football, LSU and the SEC stepped back from the expulsion brink after the Tigers confirmed they would not roster former NFL players Dae'Quan Wright and Zxavian Harris. The SEC held a Thursday videoconference in which expulsion was on the ballot but released a statement deferring final penalties. The federal lawsuit between the SEC and LSU remains active, with a hearing postponed and the scope of potential sanctions, suspension, fines, voting restrictions, still unspecified.

Elsewhere, D'Andre Swift signed a three-year, $33.75 million extension with the Chicago Bears locking him through 2029 at approximately $11.2 million per year, the 14th-ranked average annual value among NFL running backs. Swift's career-high 2025 season under new Bears coach Ben Johnson justified the investment. Former NFL running back LeShon Johnson was sentenced to five years in federal prison on September 10 for operating a large-scale dogfighting ring in Oklahoma, resulting in 190 dogs surrendered to the government, the largest number seized from one individual in a federal dogfighting case. In tennis, Elena Rybakina clinched the world No. 1 ranking by defeating Coco Gauff 3-6, 6-4, 6-4 in the US Open semifinal on September 11, setting up a final against top seed Aryna Sabalenka on Saturday, the first time the top two women's seeds have contested a US Open final since 2013. In baseball, the Rays lead the AL East by 3 games over the Yankees, the Phillies hold a 1-game lead for the first NL Wild Card over the Cubs, and the Padres lead the Diamondbacks by 0.5 games for the third NL Wild Card spot. Best-of-three Wild Card Series begin September 29.
